All locations must be in one Hetzner network zone. The default locations are all in eu-central.

#8.3 pgha estimate

Shows the estimated monthly bill. It creates nothing. It reads live prices from the Hetzner API, so it needs the token.

#8.4 pgha up

Creates the cluster.

  1. It shows the bill.
  2. It runs the SSH check on this computer, if the run adds nodes. --skip-ssh-check skips this step.
  3. It asks for confirmation. --yes skips the question.
  4. It creates the SSH key, network, firewall, volumes, servers and load balancer. --network skips network creation and uses that network.
  5. It writes the state file.
  6. It connects to every node over SSH, for up to 8 minutes, if the run added nodes. A skipped check does not skip this step.

You can run up again. It skips the resources that exist. It does not change resources that exist, with one exception: a firewall that no server uses takes the rules of this run. A later up keeps the live SSH port and refuses another one.

If a node does not answer, or a step fails after retries, up deletes the resources that this run created and then stops with the error. It never deletes:

  • resources that existed before this run, for example the nodes of a cluster that you grow, or a run that completes an earlier one;
  • a network you gave with --network;
  • an adopted server. adopt removes the labels it added and detaches the server from a network it attached.

The cleanup also runs after Ctrl+C. It has 15 minutes. If a delete fails, the error names it and says to run pgha down. --keep-on-failure keeps the new resources, for example to look at a failed server.

The load balancer joins the private network before up adds the nodes as targets. A run that completes an earlier one attaches an existing load balancer that has no network.

--monitor installs the alert timer on nodes created in this run. Read section 20. If a node already exists, up still succeeds and prints:

monitor installs on new nodes; run pgha monitor install

The servers finish installing the software after up returns. This takes about 5 minutes. Use pgha status to see when the roles show primary and replica.

--redis also runs Redis with Sentinel on every node, next to Postgres. --redis-memory-pct and --redis-policy tune it. On a cluster that has Redis, a plain up adds Redis to its new nodes; on one without Redis, use pgha redis add. pgha redis up takes the same flags and makes a cluster without Postgres. Read section 16.

--extensions timescaledb,pg_stat_statements installs catalog extensions at boot. Their libraries go into the first Patroni config, so no restart is needed later. On a live cluster, up gives new nodes the saved list and refuses new names; use pgha ext add. Read Extensions.

#8.5 pgha adopt

Builds the cluster around an existing server. Read section 21.

FlagMeaning
--serverName of the existing Hetzner Cloud server. Required.
--extra-packagesExtension packages to install on the new nodes.
--monitorInstall the alert timer. Read section 20.
--keep-on-failureKeep this run's new resources when creation fails.
--yesSkip the confirmation.

adopt rejects the backup flags, --pgbouncer and --tls optional or required. An adopted cluster uses plain connections.

#8.6 pgha status

Shows each node with its location, server status, role, addresses, SSH host and volume size. It also shows the load balancer addresses and the TLS mode.

The role comes from the load balancer health checks:

RoleMeaning
primaryThe node is the leader.
replicaThe node is a healthy replica.
startingNo health check is green yet.

#8.7 pgha down

Deletes the load balancer, servers, firewall, network and the SSH key that the tool created. A network passed with --network is not deleted.

FlagMeaning
--delete-volumesAlso delete the data volumes. All data is lost.
--delete-backupsAlso delete this cluster's pgBackRest backups and WAL archives. The bucket stays. A node must be reachable.
--yesSkip the confirmation.

Without --delete-volumes, the volumes stay and continue to cost money. Without --delete-backups, object storage files stay and continue to cost money.

down is blocked when the cluster has an adopted server.

CommandMeaning

db import <database>Create a database, then copy data from another server.
db listList the databases with size, limit and connection strings. With PgBouncer, it shows the PgBouncer and direct strings.

FlagCommandsMeaning
--publicallUse the public load balancer address in the connection strings.
--connections Ncreate, importConnection limit for this project (1 to 150).
--from URLimportSource database URL.

Database names use lower-case letters, digits and _. The first character is a letter. The names postgres, replicator, template0 and template1 are reserved.

#8.9 pgha backup

CommandMeaning
backup runStart a backup on the leader.
backup listShow the stored backups and the WAL range.
backup checkTest WAL archiving and the repository.

backup run --type accepts auto, full, diff or incr. auto makes a full backup on Sunday and a differential backup on other days.

#8.10 pgha monitor

CommandMeaning
monitor installInstall or update the alert timer on every reachable node.
monitor showPrint the stored monitoring history: latest values and peaks per node, and load balancer uptime per port. --since sets the window (default 1h, at most the history). Reads only the state store.
monitor collectSample every cluster in the background and keep the history in the state store, like the console. For hosts that run no console. --history sets how long (default 24h).
./pgha monitor show --name pgha --since 24h
./pgha monitor collect                 # runs until Ctrl-C; one per state store

Read section 20 for the checks, the webhook body, and the threshold flags. There is no monitor run command and no monitor disable command.

#8.11 pgha console

Starts the web console. With --auth token (the default) it prints a link with an access token.

--portfrom --listenBind port only. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_PORT.
--allowed-hostsnoneExtra Host names to answer, like pgha.example.com behind a proxy. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_ALLOWED_HOSTS (comma separated).
--access-tokenrandomLogin token for --auth token. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_TOKEN.
--authtokenSign-in: token, firebase or supabase. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_AUTH.
--auth-allownoneWho may sign in with firebase or supabase. Required with them. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_AUTH_ALLOW.
--auth-methodspasswordSign-in buttons: password and OAuth providers like google, github, microsoft. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_AUTH_METHODS.
--session-ttl12hHow long a sign-in lasts. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_SESSION_TTL.
--firebase-project-idnoneFirebase project ID. Also PGHA_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID.
--firebase-api-keynoneFirebase web API key (public). Also PGHA_FIREBASE_API_KEY.
--firebase-auth-domain<project>.firebaseapp.comFirebase auth domain. Also PGHA_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN.
--supabase-urlnoneSupabase project URL. Also PGHA_SUPABASE_URL.
--supabase-anon-keynoneSupabase anon or publishable key (public). Also PGHA_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.

--host and --port change one part of --listen. A flag wins over its environment variable.

To run the console in Docker, read Container image. To run it for a team on a server, read Run the console on a server.

#Sign-in

With --auth firebase or --auth supabase, the console shows a sign-in form. The browser signs in with the provider, and the console checks the token on the server:

  • Firebase: the ID token signature, issuer, audience and expiry, with Google's public keys.
  • Supabase: Supabase Auth answers GET /auth/v1/user for the token. This also checks that the session was not signed out.

Then the console sets its own session cookie for --session-ttl. The cookie key is new at each start, so a restart ends all sessions. A browser that is still signed in with the provider gets a new session without the form.

--auth-allow takes a comma separated list:

EntryAllows
ops@example.comOne email address.
@example.comEvery address at that domain (not subdomains).
*Any user of the Firebase or Supabase project.
anything elseOne provider user ID (Firebase uid, Supabase user id).

Emails count only when the provider says they are verified. Users are made and removed in the Firebase or Supabase dashboard; the console has no sign-up. If public sign-up is on in the project, do not use *.

Set up the provider:

  • Firebase: turn on the sign-in methods in Authentication, and add the console's domain to the authorized domains. localhost is there by default. OAuth sign-in opens a pop-up.
  • Supabase: turn on the providers in Authentication. For OAuth, add the console URL (for example https://pgha.example.com/) to the redirect URLs.

Scripts can call the API with Authorization: Bearer <token>: the console token, a Firebase ID token, or a Supabase access token. The access list applies.

The console logs each sign-in and each change (POST, PATCH, DELETE) with the user's email.

The global flags --token, --state-dir, --db, --mode and --ssh-identity apply too. --name has no effect; the console lists all clusters.

PageDoes
ClustersAll clusters with a pgha-cluster label, their health and running operations.
New clusterThe up form, with the live bill. Engine picks Postgres, Redis, or both; for Redis alone the Postgres sections hide and the volume default is 20 GB. With Tailscale on, it takes the API token. Encryption picks the --tls mode. SSH access shows the live SSH check, and Create waits for it. SSH port sets --ssh-port.
DashboardConnection string per database, read-write or read-only, and a download link for the cluster CA certificate when TLS is on. The Redis connection, when Redis is on. Nodes, with their Postgres and Redis roles, and load balancer. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
Databasesdb list, db create, db import, db drop, db sync. Public address shows the connection strings with the public load balancer address.
Database explorerTables and views, their columns, indexes, constraints and stats. Browse rows with filters, sorting and pages. Insert, edit and delete rows. SQL editor.
RedisWith Redis: connection strings, Sentinels, the role of each node, and Eviction and memory (redis config). Without it: Add Redis (redis add).
Backupsbackup list, backup run, backup check.
MonitoringCharts per node from the stored history (up to 24 hours), replication, running queries, and monitor install with the saved thresholds.
OperationsLive log of each background task. Duplicate on a finished create opens the new cluster form with its values.
SettingsThe engines, the TLS mode and other cluster facts. down, with or without the volumes and the backup files.

A Redis-only cluster shows only Dashboard, Redis, Operations and Settings.

Health is healthy when there is one primary and all nodes are running and in the load balancer, degraded with one primary and fewer healthy nodes, and unavailable with no primary.

Create, delete, import, backup and alert tasks run in the background, one at a time per cluster. Their time limits are the same as the CLI. When you stop the console with Ctrl+C, it waits for the running tasks.

The task history goes into the operations table, so it stays after a restart. The log is saved every 2 seconds while a task runs. A task that was running when the console died shows as failed at the next start.

A finished create task has a Duplicate button, on the task log and in Recent operations. It opens the new cluster form filled with that task's values, for a failed try or a cluster you want to make again. Nothing is created until you submit the form. S3 keys, the Tailscale token and the alert webhook are not saved with the task, so enter them again unless they come from the environment. If a cluster with the name still exists, the form picks a free name, because creating with the same name updates that cluster. Create tasks from before this feature have no saved values.

#Monitoring

The console reads every node of every cluster over SSH every 10 seconds, in the background, from the moment it starts. It needs no agent on the nodes: the console sends a short Python script that reads /proc, the local Postgres and the local Patroni API.

The samples go to the state store (SQLite, Postgres or Firestore) about once a minute, and the last 24 hours stay there. A restarted console loads them before its first sample, so the Performance tab opens with history, not an empty chart. pgha monitor show prints the same history in the terminal. Ranges: 15 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours and 24 hours. The long ranges come averaged, about 720 points per line; load balancer uptime in an averaged point is the share of checks that passed.

FlagDefaultMeaning
--metrics-history24hHow long samples are kept (env PGHA_METRICS_HISTORY).
--metrics-backgroundtrueOff: sample a cluster only while its page is open, as before, and show the saved history without adding to it (env PGHA_METRICS_BACKGROUND).

Node probes run every 10 seconds over SSH. Load balancer health comes from the Hetzner API, which allows 3600 calls an hour per project: a cluster that nobody views reads it every 2 minutes, an open page every 30 seconds, and the cluster list is read every minute, so a new cluster is sampled within a minute of its create.

Run one background sampler per state store: one console, or one pgha monitor collect. Two would probe the nodes twice and save twice. A Redis-only cluster has no Postgres to probe; only its load balancer is sampled.

GroupCharts
Load balancerConnect time through each port
PostgresTransactions, connections, active queries, cache hit ratio, rows read and written, WAL rate, replication lag, longest transaction, lock waits, rollbacks, temp files, database size, and with PgBouncer: clients and clients waiting
HostCPU, I/O wait, load, memory, data disk, disk reads and writes, network in and out

Click the expand button at the top right of a chart to open it large in a dialog. It shows the same time range and nodes, keeps updating, and has a legend. Press Esc or click the close button to close it.

Each node also gets a card with its role, Patroni state and timeline, connections, PgBouncer, memory, disk and uptime. The primary's pg_stat_replication shows how far each replica is behind.

#Load balancer

On a PgBouncer cluster made before pgha pooler harden, the load balancer's own health check only asks Patroni which role a node has. A node passes while its PgBouncer is down, and the load balancer keeps sending clients to it. Harden PgBouncer in this section fixes that (section 8.14). The Load balancer section checks what a client sees:

  • Each service, such as tcp:5432 → 6432, with the load balancer's check for every target next to the role the node reports and whether its PgBouncer answers.
  • A connection from every node through every port of the load balancer. It signs in and asks pg_is_in_recovery(), so it shows whether port 5432 reaches the primary and port 5433 a replica, and which node answered. With PgBouncer it signs in as pgbouncer; without it, as the Patroni superuser. Both passwords are already on the node. A node without them only checks that something answers the Postgres protocol.
  • A status per service, the issues behind it, the median connect time, and the share of passed checks in the time range.
StatusMeaning
HealthyClients get through to the right role.
DegradedClients get through, but something is wrong: a replica is out of rotation, or one node cannot connect.
FailedNo client gets through, the port reaches the wrong role, or the only target's PgBouncer is down.
UnknownNo node reported yet.

The load balancer state is read from the cloud every 30 seconds. Each check is one sign-in per port and node, so PgBouncer logs a few logins every 10 seconds while the page is open.

The Activity tab lists client sessions on the primary or on one node, with lock waits. Cancel stops the running query. End disconnects the session.

#Database explorer

Open a database from the Databases page, or use SQL editor.

  • Row edits find the row by its primary key. Tables without a primary key, views and foreign tables are read-only here.
  • Values travel as Postgres text and are bound as parameters. NULL and an empty string are different. On insert, columns left on DEFAULT get their default.
  • The SQL editor runs in a read-only transaction until you tick Allow writes. It runs as the postgres superuser and commits on success. It shows the last statement's result, up to 1000 rows. The timeout is 30 seconds, up to 10 minutes.
  • Writes go to the primary. Reads can also run on a replica.
  • SQL and values reach the node base64 encoded, never as shell text.

The nodes need python3 and python3-psycopg2. up and adopt install them.

The JSON API is under /api/. Each call needs the session cookie or Authorization: Bearer <token>. Requests that change data must come from the same origin. A delete needs ?confirm=<name>. A cluster delete also takes volumes=true and backups=true.

#8.12 pgha ca-cert

Prints the cluster CA certificate. Clients use it to check the server:

./pgha ca-cert --name pgha > ca.crt
psql "host=10.0.1.x dbname=shop_api user=shop_api sslmode=verify-ca sslrootcert=ca.crt"

It fails for a cluster with --tls off.

#8.13 pgha direct

Adds two load balancer ports to a PgBouncer cluster. They skip PgBouncer:

./pgha direct --name pgha
PortGoes to
5434The primary, direct to Postgres (read-write).
5435A replica, direct to Postgres (read-only).

New PgBouncer clusters get these ports when up makes the load balancer. Use this command for clusters made before. up with the same flags also adds them. The command is safe to run again. It fails on a cluster without PgBouncer. In the console, use Add direct ports on the cluster page.

#8.14 pgha pooler harden

Makes a PgBouncer cluster that runs survive a PgBouncer failure:

./pgha pooler harden --name pgha

On each node, over SSH, it:

  1. Sets systemd to restart PgBouncer when it stops (Restart=always).
  2. Sets net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind = 1, so PgBouncer binds the private address even when it starts before the network.
  3. Installs pgha-pooler-health on port 8010 and opens that port to the private network.
  4. Restarts PgBouncer one time, only if it does not answer on the private address.
  5. With alerts on, installs the alert timer again with the saved settings, so the node gets the new pool check and the PgBouncer restart.

Then the load balancer ports 5432 and 5433 use the check on port 8010. A node passes only when Patroni has the role and PgBouncer answers, so a node with a failed PgBouncer takes no clients. Ports 5434 and 5435 still ask Patroni on port 8008.

The load balancer changes only when every node is done and one node passes the primary check. If a node fails, the old check stays, and the command prints the error for each node. Fix the node and run the command again. It is safe to run again.

New PgBouncer clusters get all of this when up makes them.

In the console, the Settings page shows Load balancer check: Patroni only or Patroni and PgBouncer. Next to Patroni only, click Harden PgBouncer. The same button is in the Load balancer section of the Monitoring page. It runs the same steps as the command. If a node fails, the Settings page lists each failed node and its error.

#8.15 pgha redis

CommandWhat it does
pgha redis upCreates a Redis-only cluster. Takes the cluster flags of up; the Postgres flags are hidden. --volume-gb defaults to 20.
pgha up --redisCreates a cluster with Postgres and Redis on every node.
pgha redis addAdds Redis to a live cluster over SSH. --lb-type allows a bigger load balancer. --yes skips the question.
pgha redis statusPrints the password, URLs, master name and Sentinels.
pgha redis configPrints the eviction policy and memory cap. With --redis-policy and/or --redis-memory-pct, changes them on every node, live. A flag left out keeps its value.

Flags for redis up, up --redis and redis add:

FlagDefaultMeaning
--redis-memory-pct75 alone, 25 next to PostgresRedis memory cap, percent of server memory.
--redis-policynoevictionWhat Redis does at the cap.

See section 16.

#8.16 pgha clickhouse

CommandWhat it does
pgha clickhouse upCreates a ClickHouse cluster: 3 nodes, Keeper and a TLS load balancer. Takes the cluster flags of up; the Postgres flags are hidden. Defaults: --server-type ccx23, --volume-gb 100, --locations fsn1,nbg1,hel1.
pgha clickhouse statusPrints the nodes and the endpoints.
pgha clickhouse db create NAMEMakes a database and a user of the same name on every node. Safe to run again: the password stays.
pgha clickhouse db listPrints each database, its password and URLs.
pgha clickhouse db drop NAMEDrops the database, its data and its user. --yes skips the question.
pgha clickhouse backup runMakes a full backup now.
pgha clickhouse backup listPrints the backups in the bucket and the backup log.
pgha clickhouse backup testRestores the newest backup into a scratch database, checks it, drops it.
pgha clickhouse backup restore DATABASERestores one database on every node. --from picks a backup (default: the newest); --replace drops the live database first; --yes skips the question.

See section 17.

#8.17 pgha ext

CommandWhat it does
pgha ext listShows the catalog, then for each extension: its source, nodes with the package, preload state, and the databases that have it.
pgha ext add <ext>...Installs the packages on every node, adds libraries to the preload list, restarts Postgres if needed, then runs CREATE EXTENSION. Asks before a restart.
pgha ext remove <ext>...Runs DROP EXTENSION without CASCADE. The package and the preload list stay.
FlagCommandsMeaning
--databaseadd, removeDatabase to change. Give it more than once, or as a list. Default: the default database.
--no-restartaddInstall and set the preload list, but do not restart. Extensions that need the restart wait. Run add again to finish.
--yesaddSkip the question before a restart.

Read Extensions.

#8.18 pgha cdc

CommandWhat it does
pgha cdc up --source PG --target CHCreates a PeerDB server on the network of both clusters: 1 node, cx33, 40 GB, no load balancer. Takes the cluster flags of up; the Postgres and load balancer flags are hidden.
pgha cdc statusPrints the clusters and the mirrors with their state.
pgha cdc mirror create NAME --database DB --tables T1,T2Copies the tables, then each change. --target-db names the ClickHouse database (default: the same). --restart allows the rolling restart that turns on logical WAL. Safe to run again.
pgha cdc mirror listPrints each mirror, its databases, tables and state.
pgha cdc mirror drop NAMEStops the mirror and frees its slot on every node. The ClickHouse tables stay. --yes skips the question.

See Copy Postgres changes.
These flags work with all commands.
